actions.action: Recall whether nights were cool while the plant was outside
Check leaf undersides for webbing or spider mites
Slide plant out of pot and inspect roots and corm
If rotten, cut off rotten roots and repot into barely damp sphagnum moss
If roots healthy, mix perlite into the soil when possible
Check top 3 cm of soil and water thoroughly when dry
Empty the tray 15 minutes after watering
Move plant to bright indirect light indoors

reason: The answer gives sun scorch as the main cause and treats wet roots in dense soil only as a secondary issue, and the repot fix is conditional on finding rot (otherwise it says to keep the plant in its soil), so the diagnosis and advice are partial; its soil-check watering advice is safeguarded and not harmful.
